question.worked_solution:
First, we find the first-order derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(({x}^{2}+y)\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =2x\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${g}_{xxy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xxy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{xx}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡({y}^{2})) \\  & =4y\operatorname{cos}⁡({y}^{2})\end{aligned}
$$
